newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends lower on cash, unit returns.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends lower on cash, unit returns.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished lower Friday after choppy week on lower cash market prices and the return of several large western generating units, market sources said.
The 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear power unit in Avila Beach on the central California coast was back to full power after a repair outage that began July 2.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state is scheduled to reach full power by middle of next week following repairs to its cooling system.
The Washington Public Power Supply System unit took WNP-2 taken off line early Thursday for the repair work, but its reactor continued to operate at about 20 percent capacity.

Moreover, the 750 MW unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant may restart later today after its startup was postponed from Wednesday. The unit in Nevada tripped off Monday due to a boiler tube leak.

Monday firm, peak power prices at the Palo Verde (PV) switchyard in Arizona dropped to $30.00-32.00 a megawatt (MWh) from Thursday's $34.00-41.00, while those at the California-Oregon Border (COB) slipped to $15.50-17.00 from $17.50-18.50.
August PV futures settled down 59 cents at $35.27 after hitting a session low at $35.15.
September PV finished down 55 cents at $29.30. Deferred PV contracts ended up 15 to down 22 cents.
August COB futures settled down 23 cents at $22.68 a MWh, trimming a 81 cent loss. The contrac
September COB finished down seven cents at $22.76. Other COB months ended down 25 to up 15 cents.
With uncertainty lingering over the return of the San Onofre nuclear units and forecasts of hot weather in the Southwest, futures and cash prices surpass this week's highs, brokers and traders said.
On Wednesday, August PV posted a new life-of-contract high at $36.45 a MWh, $1.18 above today's settlement.
"People are waiting for the San Onofre units. If they don't come back on time, it could get ugly," a Houston futures trader said.
The 1,070 MW unit 2 and 1,080 MW unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in Southern California were scheduled to restart July 15 and 17, respectively.
A 750 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico will be shut today for three weeks for repairs.
Also, the 750 MW unit 1 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Ariz., will be shut from Friday night until early Monday morning for repair work.
"There's some (hot) weather coming up next week. That could push up prices," an East Coast broker said.
Forecasters called for hot, dry weather in the Southwest next week, and a warming trend to begin this weekend in the Pacific Northwest.
Temperatures along the West Coast are expected to average in the 70s-80s F, while those in the interior Southwest would run just above 100 degrees F.
